title: Honokiol and Magnolol Exert an Anti-Inflammatory Effect by Inhibiting JAK2/STAT3/IL17 Signalling in a Rat Model of Ulcerative Colitis: A Combination of Bioinformatics and Experimental Study.
authors: Cai, Zhaoxu; Lu, Shaojun; Chen, Jingan; Yang, Xiaoshan; Lu, Junlin; Feng, Changwen
journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨厚朴酚和和厚朴酚在大鼠溃疡性结肠炎模型中通过抑制JAK2/STAT3/IL17信号通路发挥抗炎作用，虽含分子对接和生物信息学，但核心是药物抗炎机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, inflammatory bowel disease with limited clinical treatment. Traditional Chinese medicinal ingredients honokiol and magnolol have potential anti-inflammatory and gastrointestinal protective effects. However, their anti-inflammatory potential has not been investigated in UC. This study hypothesized that honokiol and magnolol alleviate UC by targeting key inflammatory signalling pathways. To verify this, we established a 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfonic acid-induced UC rat model and administered honokiol and magnolol orally. The results showed that the two ingredients significantly reduced the disease activity index and colonic mucosal damage index and downregulated serum levels of pro-inflammatory factors TNF-alpha, IL-17, and CRP. Histopathological examination showed marked alleviation of colonic mucosal hyperemia, inflammatory infiltration, and ulcerative damage following honokiol and magnolol treatment. Bioinformatics analysis identified 74 UC-related targets for honokiol and 62 for magnolol, which were enriched in inflammatory response and JAK-STAT/IL-17 signalling pathways. A gradient boosting machine model was established to screen 16 shared hub targets, among which IL17A, JAK2, and STAT3 were highly correlated with immune cell infiltration. Molecular docking confirmed that honokiol and magnolol could stably bind to key proteins of the JAK-STAT pathway via noncovalent interactions with low binding energy. Immunohistochemistry and Western blot further verified that both ingredients significantly inhibited the activation of IL17A, JAK2, and STAT3 in the colonic tissues of UC rats. This study demonstrates that honokiol and magnolol exert anti-inflammatory effects in UC rats by inhibiting the JAK2/STAT3/IL17 pathway, providing a mechanistic basis and potential targets for the application of traditional Chinese medicinal ingredients in UC treatment.
abstract_zh: 溃疡性结肠炎（UC）是一种慢性炎症性肠道疾病，临床治疗手段有限。中药成分厚朴酚（honokiol）和和厚朴酚（magnolol）具有潜在的抗炎和胃肠保护作用。然而，它们在UC中的抗炎潜力尚未被研究。本研究假设厚朴酚和和厚朴酚通过靶向关键炎症信号通路来缓解UC。为验证此假设，我们建立了2,4-二硝基苯磺酸诱导的UC大鼠模型，并口服给予厚朴酚和和厚朴酚。结果显示，这两种成分显著降低了疾病活动指数和结肠黏膜损伤指数，并下调了血清中促炎因子TNF-α、IL-17和CRP的水平。组织病理学检查显示，厚朴酚和和厚朴酚治疗后，结肠黏膜充血、炎症浸润和溃疡性损伤显著减轻。生物信息学分析识别出厚朴酚的74个UC相关靶点和和厚朴酚的62个靶点，这些靶点富集于炎症反应和JAK-STAT/IL-17信号通路。建立了梯度提升机模型以筛选16个共享核心靶点，其中IL17A、JAK2和STAT3与免疫细胞浸润高度相关。分子对接证实，厚朴酚和和厚朴酚可通过非共价相互作用稳定结合JAK-STAT通路的关键蛋白，且结合能较低。免疫组织化学和Western blot进一步验证了这两种成分显著抑制了UC大鼠结肠组织中IL17A、JAK2和STAT3的激活。本研究证明，厚朴酚和和厚朴酚通过抑制JAK2/STAT3/IL17通路在UC大鼠中发挥抗炎作用，为中药成分在UC治疗中的应用提供了机制基础和潜在靶点。
